text:
alex: Heads-up — after the r3124 merge I’m seeing decode p95 jump ~18-25% on shortseq workloads in canary. Local perf runs match prod canary delta. :eyes:

maria: link?

alex: https://perf.redwood/compare?r=baseline...r3124 (summary in thread)

chris: quick question — did the batching thresholds change in the rollout?

alex: no batching config changes. suspect is kernel selector / fused-op scheduling from PR4512. flamegraph shows a bigger slice in the selector hotpath.

alex: snippet from perf dump:
```
decode() => kernel_selector() ~ 45%
  attn_fused_kernel_selector() +20% relative
  kv_cache_prefetch() +8%
```

jen: CI reported a perf regression too? Received any CI alerts?

perf-bot: CI job 7789: decode_shortseq p95 +12% vs baseline (threshold 5%). Marked as regression.

maria: ok. sounds like a real regression. We should bisect to the offending change and get a revert candidate if needed. Can we narrow to PR4512?

chris: I ran a micro-benchmark switching the selector to baseline with env var SELECT_KERNEL=baseline. P95 reverts to previous levels. So selector heuristic in PR4512 is the likely culprit.

alex: nice repro. Can you paste the perf config used?

chris: gist: 
```
bench --model small-16 --seq 64 --rps 200 --env SELECT_KERNEL=baseline
# steady-state run 120s
```

jen: immediate mitigation — can we pin canary pool to old selector binary or disable the heuristic flag? We should hold rollout until we ship a fix.

alex: deploy-bot: set canary hold on namespace redwood-canary-3?

deploy-bot: redwood-canary-3 rollout put on hold by @alex. Reason: decode p95 regression after r3124 merge.

maria: chris, can you prepare a targeted revert of the heuristic changes (not the whole fused-op PR) so we can roll the canary forward? If that’s low-risk we can avoid a full revert.

chris: will do. Plan: revert the heuristic delta in selector.c, add a short perf test in CI (shortseq p95 must be within 5%), and ship as hotfix PR4519.

alex: timeline?

chris: opening PR now, running internal perf run. If green, request approvals for emergency canary patch.

perf-bot: scheduled perf run 7790 for PR4519 (shortseq, warmup 30s, steady 120s).

jen: also add verbose logs in selector for next canary so we can capture exact decision counts. Keep logs gated behind flag.

chris: added logging flag selector.debug_decisions=true in PR4519. Will attach flamegraphs.

maria: thanks. also create an eval set to catch this in future (shortseq-append/p95). We need a regression alert in perf CI for selector ops.

alex: agreed. After PR lands and canary is stable, we can re-enable rollout and run a full traffic soak.

chris: PR opened: https://git.redwood/PR4519 — reverting selector heuristic delta, added CI perf check and debug flag. Perf run 7790 shows p95 within 2% of baseline so far.

jen: great. tagging @oncall for monitoring during patch rollout.

perf-bot: perf run 7790 complete: shortseq p95 +1.5% vs baseline (within threshold).

alex: moving to patch release candidate. Will coordinate canary unhold + small traffic increase. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

maria: follow-up: add a postmortem note in #postmortems with root cause (kernel-selector heuristic change + missing perf test). Assigning action items.

chris: noted, will author the postmortem and add regression test to perf CI.

jen: good work — quick detection and narrow revert. Keep an eye on kv-prefetch numbers in subsequent runs.

alex: closing loop here, will post final status in eng-runtime channel after rollout completes.
